## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9). The
flutter_app is the second shell (slice 5): it wires through
`flutterAppHostProfile` (lib/src/hosts/app_host_profile.dart — the app
host's own honest today-state, not the built-ins, whose cells pin the
matrix TARGET) and packages its platform tool families as a declared
`app-platform` extension — per-platform conditioning stays construction
glue in the shell, never a bare `if` around registration. Capabilities
the builder registers no tool for are declared with PRESENCE MARKER
services (`dynamicMessageSink`, `onDeviceProviderFactory`, the
`extRuntimeFactory` precedent): the host's extension carries the tool,
the marker keeps the cell honestly wired instead of run-narrowing off.
A host whose session scope differs from `ExecutionEnv.cwd` (the app's
mounted project folders) passes `sessionCwd` so the fabric groups mail by
workspace.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG (`scripts/auto_release.sh`
  via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main (gh-1522: the retired flow
  pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit per release). gh-1801: NO
  GitHub Release is created at tag-cut time (an asset-less create
  published an empty `latest` that broke `fa update`): the tag-run
  `binaries` job creates the release DRAFT-first via
  `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (curated CHANGELOG notes via
  `release_notes.sh` + a `release-draft-owner` marker), every leg attaches
  into it, and `release-provenance` publishes + flags `latest` ONLY after
  the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) is attached — `latest` never points at a
  release that cannot serve `fa update`. The git TAG is the single source
  of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` + `release-provenance`
  jobs (the release publishes at the provenance step). `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. build-macos.yml
  also packages a NON-sandboxed Fa.app DMG/ZIP per arch
  (`fa-macos-nosandbox-<arch>-<version>.dmg`, #2132): hardened-runtime-only
  entitlements pinned in `flutter_app/macos/Runner/ReleaseNoSandbox.entitlements`
  (+ Debug twin, exactly {cs.allow-jit, network.client, network.server} —
  test-pinned) and wired as the `ReleaseNoSandbox` Xcode configuration;
  `build_macos_nosandbox.sh` prunes before its re-sign (sealed tree) and
  asserts the signed entitlement set; the DMG is notarized + stapled by the
  same signed-path-gated step shape as the sandboxed DMG and rides the
  release attach path with the other DMGs (excluded from the auto-update
  stable names — the sandboxed build stays the default update feed).
  Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached

  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.

  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e

## Bench round 3 knobs (issue #1392)

The bench agent-timeout is no longer a wall-clock class: with
`FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1` a trial only dies by verdict — stall (a
≥240s inter-record gap, `FA_STALL_GAP_SEC`), or the absolute ceiling
(`FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC`, default 3600s; bench.yml pins the
tb harness cap above it, not 4x base). The watch, not the ladder, is
what decides: `FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1` alone still runs the legacy ×4
ladder — the extension-on branch ALWAYS exports the abs-ceiling knob
(`FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC`, default 3600), because
`TimeoutKnobs.watch_active` keys on a watch knob, not on the extension
flag (round-3 review: a dispatched run that sets only the extension is
a dispatched run that never watches). The harness cap around the
adapter (tb `--global-agent-timeout-sec`, harbor's per-task
`[agent] timeout_sec`) is an EXTERNAL cap, not a knob (gh-1576): both
workflows export it as `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC` (a harbor shard gets the
min of its tasks' declared timeouts via `bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py`)
and the shared `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` folds it into the deadline
via min() — fa's clock can never outlive the harness kill. When the cap
binds, the audit's `cap_resolution` block records the winning source and
both inputs; the adapter's own kill at the cap is outcome `external_cap`,
and an unsupervised external kill (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes
outcome `external_kill` (an absent export = unknown: the knobs rule
alone).

Every trial dir carries
`bench_metrics.json` (per-request wall/first-byte, ConnTrace socket
events, watchdog fires) and, on a stall, `hang-*.json` — replay one
from any machine with `scripts/replay_hang.sh <file> [url]`.
`FA_CONN_DEBUG=1` (also under `FA_PROVIDER_DEBUG`) turns on the
connection lifecycle trace in `sharedProviderHttpClient()`; live
`[fa-bench]` lines stream per-request progress to stderr while the run
is still going. URLs in trace lines have their query string stripped
and snapshot URLs mask credential-looking params (key-in-query
providers must not leak into logs); the payload snapshot is strictly
opt-in — set `FA_CONN_PAYLOAD_SNAPSHOT=<path>` to capture (the bench
workflow does, deliberately; nothing else should by default). A
stale-socket event fires only for a failure on a REUSED same-origin
pooled socket — a fresh-connect refusal is `connect_failed` and never
evicts the pool. The run report (`summary.py`) is green-with-note on
cancelled shards (`coverage: X/N`), splits latency p50/p95 by
concurrency level, and names any `agent_timeout` trial whose session
gaps never reached the stall threshold (score honesty).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, OR the body carries a well-formed
#     `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:
#   stale + pipeline (bot author or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched
drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { bucket: (
          if ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author marker_run; do
  [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
  case "$bucket" in
    fresh)
      fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
      ;;
    human)
      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))
      # Name the creating run so a RECURRING stuck draft points at its
      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name
      # it exactly (the stamping scripts write run/<id>); untagged
      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.
      run_url=""
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ]; then
        run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
      elif [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        run_url=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 1 \
          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi
      [ -n "$run_url" ] || run_url="no run on ref \`$tag\` (dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run)"
      # gh-2105: the staging draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN
      # (ci.yml's push run on the tag ref — release-provenance is the
      # sole publish point, gh-1801). When that train failed, the
      # creating run named above is NOT the broken step — the train is,
      # and a superseded failed train is never rerun
      # (verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only). Name it
      # (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) so the sweep issue points at
      # the true blocker. Any lookup failure degrades to the static
      # prose below — the delete + issue filing must never depend on
      # the diagnosis.
      train_line=""
      if [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
          --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
          --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
        failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
          ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
            | if . == null then empty else
                {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
              end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [ -n "$failed_train" ]; then
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          failed_jobs=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
            | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
          train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
          [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
          train_line="$train_line\n"
        fi
      fi
      deleted="$deleted- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n$train_line"
      deleted_tags="$deleted_tags $tag"
      ;;
  esac
done <<< "$drafts"

# ── issue lifecycle (dedup + self-closing) ─────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # echoes the issue number of the open sweep issue, or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label "$label" \
    --limit 100 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$title" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

stale_count=$((deleted_count + $(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true) ))

if [ "$stale_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  body=$(mktemp)
  {
    echo "**Sweep run:** $daily_url"
    echo "**Swept:** $deleted_count stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than $((max_age / 3600))h"
    printf '%b' "$deleted"
    [ -n "$humans" ] && { echo; echo "**Kept (human drafts, listed not deleted — E1):**"; printf '%b' "$humans"; }
    echo
    echo "**Fresh drafts (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $fresh_count — untouched (an in-flight run may own them)"
    echo
    if [ "$failed_trains" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "**Failed tag trains named above:** $failed_trains"
      echo
      echo "A stale draft whose tag train failed means the publish owner never ran — the draft was the gh-1801 staging draft and release-provenance (its sole publish point) is gated behind the failed train. Rerun the train if the tag should still ship; recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    else
      echo "A stale draft means a \`gh release create\` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step. Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily draft sweeper; auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale."
  } > "$body"
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    issue_action="commented on #$existing (still finding stale drafts)"
  else
    created_issue=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" \
      --body-file "$body" --label bug --label "$label" --assignee ai-teammate 2>/dev/null || true)
    issue_action="filed ${created_issue:-<issue creation failed>}"
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
else
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  issue_action="none needed"
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ sweep found nothing stale — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    issue_action="auto-closed #$existing (clean sweep)"
  fi
fi

# ── job summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{
  echo "### Release-draft sweeper"
  echo
  echo "Deleted **$deleted_count** stale pipeline-created draft(s) • failed tag trains named: **$failed_trains** • kept human drafts: **$(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true)** • fresh (<$((max_age / 3600))h): **$fresh_count** • issue lifecycle: $issue_action"
} >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/stdout}"

echo "sweeper: deleted=${deleted_tags# } human-kept=${human_tags# } fresh=$fresh_count issue=$issue_action"

[GOAL] Release hygiene: draft lifecycle invariant + daily sweeper, one naming scheme, truthful Latest, generated notes
CLOSED
## Goal — release hygiene: no orphan drafts, one naming scheme, truthful Latest, useful notes (today: 3-week-old draft v0.1.190 sits atop the releases page)

### Mess (evidence 2026-09-13)

- **Stale draft**: `v0.1.190` — draft since 2026-08-21 (3+ weeks), 12 assets attached, never published/deleted — it pins itself ABOVE the real Latest (v0.1.367) on the releases page.
- **Inconsistent titles**: some releases titled "Fa v0.1.362", others bare "v0.1.367" — different creation paths never agreed on one scheme (`scripts/auto_release.sh:101` uses bare `--title "v$next"`; another path uses the "Fa " prefix).
- **Useless notes**: every auto-release body is literally "Release v$next" — the page tells users nothing.
- **No lifecycle**: nothing owns a draft after creation — if its publish/attach step dies, the draft lives forever (v0.1.190 is the proof).

### Design

1. **Draft lifecycle invariant**: any pipeline step that creates a draft must end the run with it published or deleted (try/finally semantics in the workflow); a **daily sweeper** (rides daily-publish.yml) lists drafts older than 24h → deletes them + files the deduplicated self-closing issue (existing convention) so a RECURRING stuck draft names its broken step instead of rotting silently.
2. **One naming scheme**: bare `vX.Y.Z` everywhere (matches tags, matches pub.dev) — auto_release.sh, build-macos/build-mobile asset-attach paths, daily-publish all aligned; a CI lint asserts no "Fa " prefixes and no untitled releases get created.
3. **Latest policy**: the newest published full release always carries `latest` explicitly (`gh release edit --latest` after each publish — drafts and failed runs must never capture the badge).
4. **Useful notes (tier 2, same card)**: auto-release body = commit list since the previous tag (`git log --oneline prev..HEAD`, grouped fix/feat/chore by conventional prefix) — mechanical, no LLM needed; the sweeper can backfill notes for the silent "Release v$next" crowd on demand, not required.
5. **Root-cause note**: identify the code path that left v0.1.190 a draft (likely an asset-attach job creating drafts then dying mid-upload) and close THAT door specifically; run logs from 3 weeks ago are gone — the fix is the lifecycle, the RCA is the code-path audit (assert every `gh release create --draft` in the repo has its publish/delete counterpart in the same job).

## Acceptance criteria (TDD-first where CI-testable)

- **AC1** — Code-path audit test (shell-lint style over workflows/scripts): every draft-creating command is paired with publish-or-delete in the same job's failure path (static assert; fixture: a job that creates a draft and exits 1 → no draft remains, proven on a sandbox repo or mocked gh). (`UT-lifecycle`)
- **AC2** — Sweeper: fixture drafts (old/new) → old deleted + issue filed with the creating run named; new untouched; re-run idempotent (no duplicate issues — existing dedup convention). (`IT-sweep`)
- **AC3** — Naming: a release created through ANY path matches `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` title; the lint fails CI on a non-conforming creation path (test with a fixture workflow snippet). (`UT-naming`)
- **AC4** — Latest: after a publish, `gh release view --json isLatest` names the new release; after a failed run (no publish), Latest stays on the previous (never blank, never a draft). (`IT-latest`)
- **AC5** — Notes: a tag with 3 conventional commits since prev → body lists them grouped; a tag with zero commits (re-tag) → clean "no changes" body, not an empty page. (`UT-notes`)
- **AC6** — Regression: auto_release.sh's atomic push+tag flow unchanged; OIDC tag-publish path (ci.yml) untouched; existing releases not rewritten en masse (backfill is opt-in per release). (`REG-*`)

### Edge cases
- **E1** — Draft created by a HUMAN deliberately (real work in progress) → sweeper only touches drafts whose creator is github-actions bot AND age > 24h; human drafts listed in the sweep summary, never deleted.
- **E2** — Sweeper deletes a draft whose assets were the only copy of a build → acceptable (drafts are unpublished by definition; release artifacts live on published releases; documented in the card).
- **E3** — Two publish paths racing the same tag → `gh release create` idempotency (exists → edit, don't error) per path.
- **E4** — Notes generation on a tag with 200 commits → cap the list (50) with a "…and N more" line.

## Immediate one-off (owner action via me, not the bot)

Delete the stale draft `v0.1.190` now (`gh release delete v0.1.190` — the TAG and its git history stay; only the unpublished draft page + its 3-week-old assets go). Awaiting owner's "удаляй".

## References
- `scripts/auto_release.sh:90-113` (bare-title release create, `|| true` swallow), daily-publish.yml (attach paths), build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml (asset attach).
- Evidence: `gh api releases` — v0.1.190 draft 2026-08-21, 12 assets; title mix "Fa v0.1.362" vs "v0.1.367".
- Convention: daily-publish self-filing dedup issues (#161/#159).

Closes #2105
### Root Cause

Stale draft `v1.0.697` was the gh-1801 **staging draft**: the green `build-extension` leg of build-macos.yml run 42566734746 minted tag `v1.0.697` and created the draft (05:25:33Z); the tag train (ci.yml run 42567244226) then **failed its quality gate** on the sqlite3 native-assets hook brownout (single un-retried, status-blind download; every failed job in both runs carries the same bogus digest `bef140a1…` across 4 targets), so `release-provenance` — the sole publish point — never ran. A superseded failed train is never rerun (`verify_pubdev_release.sh` heals the LATEST tag only), so the draft rotted to the 24h sweeper, and the sweep issue's static prose misdirected the RCA at the creating run (its failed steps were not the blocker — the unnamed failed train was).

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: `build-macos-cli` now prewarms through the shared `sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm` composite (8-attempt ≈10 min contract) with per-arch `<arch>-macos` targets; the desktop build step's post-clean inline prewarm moves to the same hardened script (`sqlite3_native_assets_prewarm.dart --attempts 8`, `RUNNER_TEMP` copy, best-effort). These were the last legs still on the retired 3-attempt ≈3.5 min budget — below the measured 5+ min v1.0.697 storm — so the same brownout would re-strand drafts today.
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: when deleting a stale pipeline draft, the sweeper now looks up the tag's failed ci.yml push run and names it (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) in the sweep issue, replacing the misleading static prose for that case; any lookup failure degrades to today's prose and never gates the delete/issue filing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/ci_sqlite3_prewarm_guard_test.dart`: +3 pins (CLI composite wiring incl. per-arch target grammar, desktop post-clean hardened invocation, no retired-script references) — failed RED before the fix.
- `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: +4 sweeper cases (failed train named in the issue, green train keeps the create-death prose, unreadable lookup degrades gracefully, fresh/human drafts never trigger a lookup) — failed RED before the fix.
- Full suite: 2394 tests, 0 failures.

### Notes

- The sweeper keeps deleting the stale draft (by design); the change is diagnostic — the recurrence trigger itself is closed by keeping the release legs on the hardened prewarm contract.
- The sqlite3 hook download class was already fixed for hosted legs post-incident (gh-2072/2074/2075); this completes the release-train legs the incident actually red'd.
- No new permissions needed: `sweep-drafts` already carries `actions: read` (enforced by the stub-permission tests).

post_install do |installer|
  installer.pods_project.targets.each do |target|
    flutter_additional_ios_build_settings(target)
  end

  # wasm_run FFI symbols live in a static library inside WasmRun.xcframework.
  # They are referenced only from Dart via dlsym (DynamicLibrary.executable()),
  # so the linker never pulls them in: force_load alone is not enough because
  # DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=YES (Release default) still discards the unreferenced
  # code, and dlsym only sees exported symbols. Exporting a symbol makes it
  # both dlsym-visible AND a dead-strip root, so export every C-ABI symbol the
  # Dart bindings look up (wire_*/new_*/drop_*/…), derived from the archive
  # itself so the list stays in sync with the vendored package. Without this
  # the Release/TestFlight binary boots to a white screen
  # ("Unsupported desktop platform: ios" from wasm_run's library locator).
  # SRCROOT is the ios/ directory, so ../../ walks up to the repo root where
  # vendor/ lives.
  xcframework = '$(SRCROOT)/../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework'
  device_slice = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64/libwasm_run_dart.a"
  simulator_slice = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libwasm_run_dart.a"
  device_archive = File.expand_path('../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/ios-arm64/libwasm_run_dart.a', __dir__)
  ffi_symbols = `nm -gU -arch arm64 #{device_archive}`.lines
    .map(&:split)
    .select { |cols| %w[T D S].include?(cols[1]) && cols[2] }
    .map { |cols| cols[2] }
    .uniq
    .grep(/^_(wire|new|drop|free|get|store|init|inflate|share)_/)
    .sort
  raise "no wasm_run FFI symbols found in #{device_archive}" if ffi_symbols.empty?
  export_flags = ffi_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-exported_symbol,#{s}" }
  installer.aggregate_targets.each do |aggregate_target|
    aggregate_target.user_project.targets.each do |target|
      next unless target.name == 'Runner'
      target.build_configurations.each do |config|
        # Archive/install builds run `strip` per STRIP_STYLE. The default
        # "all" removes the dyld exports trie entirely (verified: plain
        # `strip` drops every exported wire_* symbol), which kills the
        # dlsym-based wasm_run lookups at runtime — TestFlight white screen.
        # "non-global" (strip -x) keeps the trie intact.
        config.build_settings['STRIP_STYLE'] = 'non-global'
        { 'iphoneos*' => device_slice, 'iphonesimulator*' => simulator_slice }.each do |sdk, slice|
          key = "OTHER_LDFLAGS[sdk=#{sdk}]"
          ldflags = Array(config.build_settings[key] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
          # Drop stale wasm_run flags from earlier pod installs.
          ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
          ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{slice}"
          # cupertino_http (the NSURLSession-backed HTTP client on iOS)
          # ships its FFI trampolines (_NativeCupertinoHttp_*) in a static
          # pod framework. Nothing native references them, so the Release
          # link dead-strips the archive members and Dart's dlsym lookup
          # fails at runtime ('No asset with id package:cupertino_http/
          # src/native_cupertino_bindings.dart found') — every network call
          # errors out. Same failure class as the wasm_run white screen.
          #
          # The fix is -exported_symbol, NOT force_load: an exported symbol
          # must exist in the output, so ld pulls the defining archive
          # member AND keeps it in the exports trie (which is what dlsym
          # reads). force_load of the same archive the pod already links
          # via -framework would double-include the dummy object
          # (duplicate PodsDummy_cupertino_http) — and breaking the
          # -framework flag instead would drop the pod-target build
          # ordering ('Build input file cannot be found' under gym's
          # archive build). Both failure modes seen on CI.
          #
          # The symbols are derived from the plugin's generated bindings
          # source (C names gain one Mach-O underscore, hence the extra '_').
          # Drop cupertino_http force_load flags injected by earlier
          # Podfile revisions — exported_symbol alone is the fix now.
          ldflags.reject! { |f| f.include?('cupertino_http') && f.start_with?('-Wl,-force_load') }
          cupertino_src = File.expand_path(
            '.symlinks/plugins/cupertino_http/darwin/cupertino_http/Sources/cupertino_http/native_cupertino_bindings.m',
            __dir__,
          )
          cupertino_symbols = File.read(cupertino_src)
            .scan(/\b_NativeCupertinoHttp_\w+/)
            .uniq
            .sort
          raise "no _NativeCupertinoHttp_* symbols found in #{cupertino_src}" if cupertino_symbols.empty?
          cupertino_export_flags = cupertino_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-exported_symbol,_#{s}" }
          ldflags.reject! { |f| f.include?('_NativeCupertinoHttp_') }
          if config.name == 'Debug'
            # Debug must NOT get -exported_symbol flags: giving any flips ld
            # into "export only these" mode, which hides the JIT entry point
            # (main) from the debug host — abort_could_not_find_entry_point
            # at launch. But WITHOUT any flag the trampoline archive members
            # are never pulled either (nothing native references them), so
            # Dart's dlsym fallback fails at runtime even in Debug.
            # -Wl,-u,<sym> forces the defining members into the link while
            # leaving the default "export all globals" trie intact.
            ldflags.concat(cupertino_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-u,_#{s}" })
          else
            ldflags.concat(cupertino_export_flags)
          end
          ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
          config.build_settings[key] = ldflags
        end

        # gh-2106: CocoaPods turns the vendored archive-slice XCFramework
        # into -l"wasm_run_dart" on the Runner link (Pods-Runner.*.xcconfig
        # OTHER_LDFLAGS), resolved ONLY through LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS'
        # ${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter — a copy the
        # wasm_run_flutter pod's "[CP] Copy XCFrameworks" phase rsyncs at
        # BUILD time. That phase's DECLARED output
        # (…/XCFrameworkIntermediates/wasm_run_flutter/WasmRun.framework)
        # never matches the real artifact (the slices ship a bare
        # libwasm_run_dart.a, no framework bundle), so on a self-hosted
        # runner a cancelled build can poison the per-project DerivedData
        # build database (~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData — keyed by
        # the checkout path, OUTSIDE the repo, invisible to the workspace
        # `git clean -ffdx`) and every later run skips the copy; the link
        # then dies with "Library 'wasm_run_dart' not found"
        # (v1.0.707, run 42965479924: 6/6 fa-m5-2 runs red since the
        # cancelled 20:45 dispatch, same tree green on fa-m5-1 and hosted).
        # Point the -l straight at the restored slices — the same paths the
        # force_load flags and the post_install nm check already pin — so
        # the link no longer depends on the intermediates copy at all.
        # Search order puts the vendor slice before $(inherited) so a
        # stale intermediates copy can never satisfy the -l lookup with
        # different bytes than the force_load loaded.
        device_slice_dir = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64"
        simulator_slice_dir = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator"
        { 'iphoneos*' => device_slice_dir, 'iphonesimulator*' => simulator_slice_dir }.each do |sdk, slice_dir|
          key = "LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=#{sdk}]"
          paths = Array(config.build_settings[key] || []).dup
          # Drop flags injected by earlier pod installs (idempotent re-runs).
          paths.reject! { |p| p.include?('WasmRun.xcframework') }
          paths.reject! { |p| p == '$(inherited)' }
          config.build_settings[key] = [slice_dir, '$(inherited)', *paths]
        end
      end
    end
  end

content.text: (empty = releases fully deleted)

# activity/session rows render fixed instants in the OS-local
        # zone; baselines embed UTC renderings, the runner's zone must
        # match or the helper fails loudly.
        env:
          TZ: UTC
        run: flutter test test/golden
      # flutter_test writes the expected/actual/diff triple for every
      # failed comparison into goldens/failures/ — upload them so a
      # hosted-vs-capture drift can be EYEBALLED from the artifacts
      # instead of triangulated from percentages (the 2026-11-10
      # activity-golden red that passed locally).
      - name: Upload golden failure diffs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: golden-failure-diffs
          # flutter_test writes the failure triple relative to the TEST
          # dir (test/golden/failures/), not the goldens/ dir.
          path: flutter_app/test/golden/failures/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  flutter-app-lock-smoke:
    name: Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: >-
...
          # gh-2042 AC1: the immutability gate owns the attach (published
          # releases are immutable for fa-* assets — skip/refuse, never clobber).
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" fa-web-spa.zip

      # continue-on-error keeps the job/check green even on failure — a
      # release can then only be gated on a MISSING asset. Surface the miss
      # in the run's step summary too (covers upload flakes, not just guard
      # trips); the failed steps remain visible in the job view.
      - name: Flag missing bundle in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-web-spa.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The web SPA bundle job failed (continue-on-error: the release ships without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # gh-1847: the tag train builds fa-extension.zip ITSELF. The leg
  # mirrors web-spa (additive attach, quality-gate keyed) because the
  # failure mode it kills is identical in shape: the extension's former
  # ONLY producer was build-macos.yml build-extension, a once-daily leg
...
          # unattached fa-* assets loud, and re-signing goes through
          # release-provenance only.
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" "$asset"

      # Mirror of the web-spa summary flag: surface the miss in the run's
      # step summary (covers build/size-gate/upload flakes); the failed
      # steps remain visible in the job view. The release-provenance
      # required-assets gate is what actually blocks the publish.
      - name: Flag missing extension in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-extension.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The extension build job failed (continue-on-error: the gh-1832 gate strands the release without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # SEC-07 (#795): the installer's default trust path is SIGNED checksums.
  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) and build-extension
  # (gh-1847, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web bundle and
  # the extension zip cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering
  # makes the fa-* sweep deterministic — web-spa/extension success ->
  # zip signed, failure -> zip absent — never a half-updated manifest,
  # and the gh-1832 gate below never races a slow attach.

Closes #2106
### Root Cause

`Build iOS (debug, unsigned)` red on every self-hosted `fa-m5-2` run since the cancelled 2026-11-10 20:45 dispatch (6/6 runs, three different trees — green on `fa-m5-1` and GitHub-hosted with the identical v1.0.707 tree) with `Error (Xcode): Library 'wasm_run_dart' not found`. CocoaPods generates `-l"wasm_run_dart"` on the Runner link (from the vendored archive-slice `WasmRun.xcframework`), and its only search path is `${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter` — a copy made at BUILD time by the pod's `[CP] Copy XCFrameworks` phase, whose declared output (`…/WasmRun.framework`) never matches the real bare-`.a` slice. That copy's build bookkeeping lives in a DerivedData build database outside the repo (survives the workspace `git clean -ffdx`, keyed per checkout path → per runner); the cancelled run poisoned `fa-m5-2`'s, the copy stopped landing, the `-l` lookup failed, the link died.

### Fix

- `flutter_app/ios/Podfile`: the `post_install` hook now also injects `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=iphoneos*]` / `[sdk=iphonesimulator*]` pointing at the restored `WasmRun.xcframework` slice dirs (vendored path first, before `$(inherited)`) — the same paths the existing `-Wl,-force_load` flags and the post_install `nm` check already pin — so ld resolves `-l"wasm_run_dart"` from the restored archive and never depends on the intermediates copy.
- `flutter_app/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`: regenerated via `pod install` and committed (pod-install-stable; carries the new settings for Debug/Release/Profile).
- `test/wasmrun_ios_pod_link_test.dart`: n

- name: flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)
        # E2, corrected by gh-1296: classify the failure by EVIDENCE in the
        # log, not by a blanket keyword. The old grep matched 'cocoapods' or
        # 'pod install' in EVERY flutter iOS build log ("Running pod
        # install… 4.4s" prints even on green builds), so every failure was
        # mislabeled "CocoaPods layer — likely spec drift" — that
        # mislabeling sent gh-1296 at a Podfile.lock fix while the real
        # killer was a package build hook (sqlite3's native-assets download
        # hash check). Most-specific layer first; unmatched failures stay
        # unlabeled rather than guessed.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          cd flutter_app
          # SDK-train moves regenerate Flutter.framework/Headers, and the
          # self-hosted box's Xcode DerivedData keeps SwiftExplicitPrecompiledModules
          # .pcm files built against the PREVIOUS train's headers — the next
          # build dies with "FlutterPlugin.h has been modified since the
          # module file was built". Wipe the Runner scheme's DerivedData
          # before building (cheap: the pod/Xcode caches live elsewhere).
          # gh-2134: the old wipe was a HOME-global glob
          # (`rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-*`) — and
          # the fa-m5 pool is ONE box (one $HOME) hosting MULTIPLE
          # concurrent runner processes (fa-m5-1/2/3). Run 43203130726
          # (v1.0.712) died exactly that way: the sibling run 43202707134's
          # wipe on fa-m5-2 (10:55:32) deleted THIS leg's live DerivedData
          # on fa-m5-1 mid-xcodebuild → "accessing build database … disk
          # I/O error" + vanished Runner-OutputFileMap.json. The DerivedData
          # dir hash is keyed to the checkout path, so each runner process
          # owns a private dir — scope the wipe by the owner recorded in
          # each Runner-*/info.plist WorkspacePath: only the dir whose
          # WorkspacePath resolves to THIS checkout's workspace is removed
          # (both spellings are compared — raw and symlink-resolved — so a
          # concurrent leg's dir can never match; a dir with no readable
          # info.plist may be a live early build and is left alone; the
          # PlistBuddy error text that lands on STDOUT is filtered from
          # $ws before any branch sees it). Dirs whose recorded
          # WorkspacePath no longer exists on disk (dead checkout:
          # re-registered runner, renumbered _work, deleted branch) are
          # swept as orphans — race-free, a live leg's checkout always
          # exists. Every removal, every kept dir, and a no-candidate pass
          # log a `gh-2134:` line — a silent no-op must be diagnosable
          # from CI logs (run 43204833 kept its own dir on a
          # resolved-vs-logical divergence with zero signal). Pinned by
          # test/ci_build_ios_derivedata_wipe_guard_test.dart.
          ws_path="$(pwd -P)/ios/Runner.xcworkspace"
          shopt -s nullglob
          matched=
          for dd in ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-*/; do
            ws=$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :WorkspacePath' "$dd/info.plist" 2>/dev/null || true)
            # PlistBuddy prints its error text on STDOUT (the 2>/dev/null
            # above cannot suppress it): "File Doesn't Exist, Will
            # Create: …" for a missing plist, "Print: Entry,
            # :WorkspacePath, Does Not Exist" for a keyless one. Run
            # 43204833 captured that text into $ws and the orphan sweep
            # below then removed two plist-less (maybe-live early-build)
            # dirs. Keep only absolute-path values.
            case "$ws" in
              /*) ;;
              *) ws= ;;
            esac
            # gh-2136 rework (run 43204833): the recorded WorkspacePath
            # can spell the SAME directory differently than this step's
            # `pwd` — a symlinked runner-path component makes Xcode
            # record the resolved path while `$(pwd)` reports the logical
            # one. That run's own dir Runner-bdeltrtwvfjmnocetzuxfpyqvkmk
            # (still carrying the earlier incident's corrupted build.db)
            # was seen but silently kept on exactly this divergence, and
            # the xcodebuild died on it 13 min later with the same
            # disk-I/O signature. Normalize both spellings before
            # comparing (`cd + pwd -P` resolves the recorded value).
            ws_res="$(cd "$ws" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P || true)"
            if [ "$ws" = "$ws_path" ] || [ "$ws_res" = "$ws_path" ]; then
              echo "gh-2134: wiping DerivedData owned by this workspace: $dd"
              rm -rf "$dd"
              matched=1

**Already fixed in current code** (no code change made, no PR):
- Root cause closed by PR #2109 (merge commit `2a380b2`, merged 2026-11-11T07:39:51Z — BEFORE this ticket was filed on 2026-11-13T05:19): `flutter_app/ios/Podfile` `post_install` now pins `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=iphoneos*|iphonesimulator*]` at the restored vendored slice dirs ahead of `$(inherited)`, so the `-l"wasm_run_dart"` lookup no longer depends on the intermediates copy; regenerated pbxproj committed. tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout.
